desc: Derive/verify the lower-bound argument: each value must cross every boundary between its start and final position at least once, and a constructive sequence achieves exactly those crossings (samples give 4, 6, 0).
Implement range-add via difference array: for each value v at position p, let l=min(v,p), r=max(v,p)-1; if l<=r do diff[l]+=1, diff[r+1]-=1, then answer = sum_i i*cnt[i].
Implement O(N) solution: read N and permutation, build pos array, build diff array of size N+2, prefix-sum to get cnt[i] per boundary, compute ans = sum(i*cnt[i] for i in 1..N-1).
Validate with brute force (Dijkstra over permutation state graph) for N<=7 exhaustive and N=8 random against the formula; all matched, including samples 4, 6, 0.
Final Python solution uses fast I/O (sys.stdin.buffer) and Python ints for the ~1e15-scale answer.
